issues.text: All 17 assigned records were read in full, including every retained body paragraph and every editorial footnote. The packet is a pinned candidate set, not an exhaustive archive search.

Composition dates of incoming Kemp letters do not establish Darwin's receipt. The knowledge_before dates 1843-10-09, 1843-11-09, and 1843-12-07 are conservative bounds from sufficiently dated Darwin writings.

Most outgoing dates include editorially supplied components. 565F has an especially unstable/nuanced header and date note; 711F is reconstructed from the 4 and 10 November exchange; 716F preserves Darwin's apparent 'Nov. 31.' writing while editorially dating it 1 December.

565F is marked 4pp inc and the preserved body ends mid-sentence. Its header/date readings ('1[1] May [1840]' and 'Monday May 1⟨8⟩' versus the note's post-conservation 'Monday May 10', presumed May 11) should not be treated as a complete stable prompt.
720 is marked 2pp encl. Certificates/testimonials are referenced but not reconstructed; no content from those enclosures was invented or treated as full-text evidence.
Incoming records are Kemp voice throughout. Darwin's letters report or quote Lindley, Henslow, Babington, Brown, and other sources; those third-party voices remain separately attributed.
Darwin's paper/abstract draws from multiple Kemp letters and adds remarks of his own. A future prompt must preserve the boundary between Kemp-supplied facts and Darwin's editorial additions.
Several direct references require full-text reading of records outside this packet before using them as evidence: DCP-LETT-562G, 668, 669, 691, 701, 705, 707, 708, 712, and 579.
